clue.text: One who does us redraft specially

definitions.note: to do someone is slang for to cheat them

indicators.note: specially suggests something made to order, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone tells us they are rewriting a document especially for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is the slang verb for cheating, not the plain auxiliary it pretends to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is someone who cons or cheats people, which is what 'does' means in slang.

clue.text: Price trainer perhaps quoted for shawl

indicators.note: quoted means spoken by someone, so the letters are what that pair sounds like

parts.note: a price is a fee and a trainer is a kind of shoe

explanation.surface: A sports shoe's cost is cited for a wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: FEE plus SHOE, said together, give the French name of a lady's triangular neck scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular scarf or shawl worn round the shoulders and neck.

clue.text: Clown in funny hat, etc, and toga?

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: read backwards as a clue, giddy goat is a jumbled goat, which gives the Roman garment; the question mark flags that reverse reading

explanation.surface: Someone acts the fool wearing a silly hat and a Roman robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges HAT ETC to ACT THE; then GIDDY GOAT is read as an instruction (giddy = anagram of GOAT) that yields TOGA, so the clue gives the result, not the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To clown about is to behave in a silly, frivolous way, which the idiom describes.

clue.text: Abusive words stain a family broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the pieces are heard rather than read

parts.note: to dye is to stain, and a family is a tribe

explanation.surface: Insults that tarnish a whole household are put on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a tirade of abuse.

clue.text: Watch what joy rider would do, ending in trouble

parts.note: a joyrider steals a vehicle for fun, so takes a car

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Beware of what a car thief does, since it ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending in trouble' gives E, the last letter of 'trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: Watch, as in 'watch out', is a warning to be careful.

clue.text: Like most recent recruits, perhaps, artillerymen need direction

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
west is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Newly enlisted gunners need guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks that the newest recruits are only an example of the most inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw means green and inexperienced, so the freshest recruits are typically the least seasoned.

clue.text: Face protection racket or swindle in village: heads must roll!

indicators.note: rolling the picked letters over turns their order backwards
the heads of the words are their opening letters, taken from each in turn

explanation.surface: A rural scam is exposed and the villagers demand that someone pay with their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes R, O, S, I, V from the five words and 'must roll' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is the movable front of a helmet that shields the wearer's face.

clue.text: Very small drink for taking neat in the opinion of many

indicators.note: taking means the first pieces hold this one inside them

parts.note: V is short for very, so very small is a single letter
pop is a fizzy soft drink
neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one

explanation.surface: Many people think a tiny tot is best drunk undiluted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' means cattle, not undiluted, and 'Very small' is just V.
explanation.definitionFit: A vox pop, from Latin vox populi, is a sampling of public views, the voice of the people.

clue.text: Twin evils fashion captivating fellow's character, in the main

parts.note: two kinds of wickedness: a sin and something bad
two kinds of wickedness: a sin and something bad

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to tailor something is to fashion or shape it
he's, the fellow is

explanation.surface: Two wicked twins design something to charm a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twin evils' looks like the definition; it is wordplay, and 'the main' is the open sea, so the character is a seafarer. 'captivating' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad the Sailor is the seafaring hero of the Arabian Nights tales, a character at sea.

clue.text: Copper to arrest one drunk at cocktail party?

parts.note: rusty describes a reddish-brown, copper colour
to nail someone is to catch or arrest them

explanation.surface: A policeman is told to arrest a tipsy guest at a drinks party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman and 'drunk' a drunkard; one is a colour and the other a drink consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusty nail is a cocktail of Scotch whisky and Drambuie, something drunk at such a party.

clue.text: Back law tackling receding hems in parade ground

indicators.note: receding says the hidden letters are read backwards
to hem something in is to enclose it, so the run is held within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone backing a law about tackling, with a sewing aside, on a drill square.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'hems in' as part of the definition; it is the hiding signal, leaving 'parade ground' alone to define. 'receding' reverses KLAWTAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A catwalk is the runway on which fashion models parade, so it is a ground for parading.

clue.text: Small dogs apparently getting more substantial hair removal treatments

indicators.note: to dog someone is to follow close behind, so this letter comes after the word

parts.note: waxing describes a moon growing larger, so becoming bigger

explanation.surface: Little dogs seem to be growing plumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' looks like a noun after 'Small', but it is a verb: S follows (dogs) WAXING. 'apparently' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Waxings are beauty sessions in which hot wax is spread on the skin and pulled off to strip unwanted hair.

clue.text: Guide hard for operator to grasp

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: someone who operates a machine or computer is its user
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough concept for a machine operator to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, so leading or guiding them is the job.

clue.text: Winger very cautious on short pitch

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to pitch is to throw or cast
so is an informal intensifier meaning very
wary means cautious or on guard

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing takes great care on a pitch that is too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer on the wing; here it is a bird. CAST cut short gives CAS. The cassowary cannot fly, so the definition is loose, but it has (small) wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The cassowary is a large flightless Australasian bird, and any bird can be loosely called a winged creature.

clue.text: One tweeting often shut up about bridge thrashing

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: a thrashing knocks something about, so the word's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone constantly posting online is told to be quiet about a losing night at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweeting' and 'shut up' suggest a social-media user being silenced; they describe a songbird kept caged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet songbird kept in a cage sings or chirps and is confined there most of the time.

clue.text: Bishop who helps a court judge do tours

indicators.note: a tour goes round about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A judge from a court goes travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tours' is the anagram signal on A, COURT, J and DO together.
explanation.definitionFit: A coadjutor is a bishop appointed to assist a diocesan bishop, often with right of succession.

clue.text: Series of columns from a poetess regularly recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the chosen letters come back in reverse order
regularly means taking every other letter at even spacing

explanation.surface: Lines of verse quoted from a poet, remembered at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks A, O, T, S from 'a poetess'; 'recalled' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a classical Greek portico, a covered walkway lined by a row of pillars.

clue.text: What's borne primarily in message of distress by one who's blue?

definitions.text: What's borne primarily in message of distress by one who's blue?

indicators.note: the letter sits within the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the word supplies its first letter

parts.note: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, whose members are Tories

explanation.surface: A distress message sent by a sad person.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservatives. Read whole, the clue describes a hard-luck tale from someone feeling blue; 'primarily' and 'in' are the selection and containment signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a sad tale told to win sympathy, the kind of thing a miserable person bears.

clue.text: Criticising valuable diamond, perhaps, after turning up nose

indicators.note: the card comes after the other piece
in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: conk is slang for nose
the king of diamonds is a high, valuable playing card

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a precious gem with nose in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'valuable diamond' suggests a gem, but it is a high card of the diamond suit. 'turning up' reverses the slang word for nose, and 'after' places the card behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking means disparaging or running down, as in knocking copy.

clue.text: Chap who'd be skilful on horse

indicators.note: the name with H set on it would be the word for skilful, so here H is taken off

parts.note: handy means skilful or dexterous
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A man who would be a fine rider if put in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Put H (horse, slang for heroin) on the name and it becomes HANDY, skilful; so the name is that word without H.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy is a common man's name, and crosswords use a first name to stand for any chap.

clue.text: Someone who was hunting for Auntie's old record player

definitions.meaning: a Cumbrian huntsman celebrated in the song D'ye ken?
a long-serving BBC Radio 1 disc jockey; Auntie is a nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: A huntsman who once spun discs for the BBC.
explanation.walkthrough: Two men with one name: the huntsman of the folk song 'D'ye ken John Peel' and the late BBC DJ. 'Auntie' is British slang for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a famous Lakeland huntsman and a famous BBC radio DJ carried this name.

clue.text: As example, Moray invested in accommodation for Tamworth firm

indicators.note: invested means put inside, so this piece goes within the other

parts.note: a Tamworth is a breed of pig, and a pig lives in a sty
a moray is a kind of eel

explanation.surface: Someone called Moray has put money into housing for a firm in the town of Tamworth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a Midlands town but here the British pig breed named after it; Moray is a Scottish region but here the eel.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard and resolute, like steel, so unyielding or firm.

clue.text: Part of neck that is showing above fancy collar

indicators.note: in a down clue this piece is placed above the other

parts.note: sc, from scilicet, means namely or that is to say
a ruff is an ornate pleated collar

explanation.surface: A bit of the throat peeks out above an elaborate collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is usually IE; here it is SC, scilicet.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, as in being taken by the scruff.

clue.text: Levers bears on to transport

indicators.note: this piece is placed on to the end of the other

parts.note: a transport of delight is great joy
to stick something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: Bears clamber aboard a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' means rapture, not a vehicle, and 'bears' is a verb, not animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Joysticks are control levers, as in an aircraft cockpit or a games controller.

clue.text: Fools trapped in fraction of a metre gap

indicators.note: these letters are caught inside the other piece

parts.note: a centimetre, abbreviated CM, is a hundredth of a metre
to have someone is to fool them, so has means fools

explanation.surface: Silly people stuck in a tiny space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fools' looks like a plural noun but is a verb: HAS, as in 'you've been had'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep fissure or yawning gap in the ground.

clue.text: Foreign letter copied from the original notes

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic marks a quotation copied exactly as in the original

explanation.surface: A letter from abroad reproduced exactly from the first version.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is written in notes, so a collection of notes stands for it.

clue.text: American writer's touching article that bores you

indicators.note: boring into something means drilling inside it, so this pair goes within the other word

parts.note: thou is the old form of you
re means concerning or touching on
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about an American author that turns out to be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bores' looks like tedium, but RE and A drill into THOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau was the nineteenth-century American author of Walden.

clue.text: Bugs chasing and overtaking old birds

annotationWithheld.why: Bugs chasing and overtaking old birds (7): the parse is O + RI(O)LES, which needs two Os, but 'old' is the only word to give one, so it does two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Bugs chasing and overtaking old birds

clue.text: Cross desert from the east yet avoiding interior

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray

indicators.note: in an across clue reading from the east means right to left, so these letters go backwards
the middle is skipped, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone angry crosses a desert heading west, yet skirts the middle of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding interior' keeps Y and T of 'yet'; 'from the east' turns them to TY. 'desert' is a verb, not sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is informal British for irritable or bad-tempered, the same as cross.

clue.text: Fair clay: good ground for toadstool

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Fine clay makes a decent soil for growing a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil, but it is the past tense of grind, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The fly agaric is the red, white-spotted poisonous fungus of fairy-tale illustrations.
